title: "Tool 2 — RBIG Forward & Backward"
subtitle: "marginal + rotation, iterated · sampling"

*Learn-the-tool track · Lab 2 of 3.*

Run the full machine: forward to a spherical Gaussian, backward to new samples.
You will check both directions on a controlled co-crashing pair.

---

## 1 · Forward — does it Gaussianize?

::: {#91df88e3 .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
a, b = datasets.tail_dependent_pair(n=2000, seed=1)
X = np.column_stack([a, b])
rbig = AnnealedRBIG(n_layers=30, random_state=0).fit(X)
Z = rbig.transform(X)

print(f"data  |corr| = {abs(np.corrcoef(a, b)[0,1]):.3f}   co-crash = {cocrash_fraction(a,b):.0%}")
print(f"RBIG  |corr| = {abs(np.corrcoef(Z[:,0], Z[:,1])[0,1]):.3f}   "
      f"marginal std = {Z.std(0).round(2)}")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}
```
data  |corr| = 0.806   co-crash = 57%
RBIG  |corr| = 0.000   marginal std = [1. 1.]
```
:::
:::


---

## 2 · Backward — does it generate?

::: {#d2bc8150 .cell execution_count=3}
``` {.python .cell-code}
gen = rbig.sample(2000)
print(f"real co-crash      = {cocrash_fraction(a, b):.0%}")
print(f"generated co-crash = {cocrash_fraction(gen[:,0], gen[:,1]):.0%}   ← tail dependence regenerated")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}
```
real co-crash      = 57%
generated co-crash = 58%   ← tail dependence regenerated
```
:::
:::


::: {#cell-fig-tool2-rbig .cell execution_count=4}
``` {.python .cell-code}
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(13, 4.2))
for ax, data, col, title in [
```

## 3 · How many layers?

::: {#6ac36737 .cell execution_count=5}
``` {.python .cell-code}
print("layers   |corr| after forward")
for L in [1, 2, 5, 15, 30]:
    Zl = AnnealedRBIG(n_layers=L, random_state=0).fit_transform(X)
    print(f"  {L:>3d}      {abs(np.corrcoef(Zl[:,0], Zl[:,1])[0,1]):.3f}")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}
```
layers   |corr| after forward
    1      0.000
    2      0.000
    5      0.000
   15      0.000
   30      0.000
```
:::
:::


::: {.callout-tip}
## What to look for
For a 2-D pair, PCA rotation decorrelates fast — but *decorrelated is not
independent*.  The co-crash check (a tail-dependence probe) is the honest test of
whether the joint is truly Gaussian, and it is what the backward pass must
reproduce.
:::
